gaps.sentence: I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: I can't imagine ___ in a tiny village again.
The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: We can't risk ___ the connection flight.
After introducing herself, she went on ___ the main findings.
gaps.hint: move on to a new activity
gaps.explanation: go on + to-infinitive = do something after finishing something else.

gaps.sentence: Remember ___ your passport to the airport.
gaps.explanation: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something.
